modelImitationOnFixedCode.finding: The model still imitates on the fixed code, and the fix holds anyway. In the headless leg the model itself supplied an `env` object on 26 of 31 calls (every call from 6 onward): all six of the hook's keys copied verbatim (GH_CONFIG_DIR and PATH exact, the token keys empty) with a fabricated v4-shaped LEGION_GRANT that was never minted (26 of 26). This is visible in the streamed toolcall_end events in events.jsonl (the model's arguments before the hook) versus the persisted transcript (after the hook). Because the hook spreads its keys last, the persisted and executed env.LEGION_GRANT equals the hook's mint on all 26, every record-grant ran under the mint, and every redemption was 200. The terminal leg showed the same: the tmux pane rendered call 5 as `LEGION_GRANT="b3c1b7a0-84d1-4f22-9d8f-c" record-grant; echo step-6` (the model's streamed env, a truncated fabrication) while the persisted call carries the hook's 8659b844... and seen-grants.log shows the command ran under 8659b844.... This is the live case for the spec's precedence requirement, beyond regression test B.
modelImitationOnFixedCode.commandTextStaysClean: On neither fixed leg did the model ever put the credential into the command text (0 occurrences of LEGION_GRANT in 39 persisted commands); the imitation moved entirely into the env object, where the hook wins.

standIn.rule: Verified against a fresh stand-in on port 13498: a minted grant redeemed 200 five times within 0.2 s (gh-token x3, git-credential, phase/complete) -> not single-use; the same id 38 s after mint -> 200; at 101 s -> 403 `Invalid or expired grant` on gh-token, git-credential, and phase/complete. A fabricated id -> 403 `Invalid or expired grant`; a mint with a wrong session secret -> 403 `Invalid session secret`.
